**Solution 1** gets the right magnitude, 2431/50, but the wrong sign. The correct value is **−2431/50**.

Let g(x) = x²f(x) − 1, a degree-9 polynomial with roots at s_n = n(n+1) for n = 1,…,8. Write g(x) = c(x − a)p(x), where p(x) = ∏(x − s_n).

- **Finding a:** Since x²f(x) = g(x) + 1 must be divisible by x², we need g'(0) = 0. Using p'(0)/p(0) = −Σ1/s_n = −8/9 (telescoping), this gives a = −9/8.
- **Finding c:** g(0) = −1 gives c(9/8)p(0) = −1, with p(0) = 8!·9! > 0. So c = −8/(9·8!·9!) < 0.
- **Evaluating at 90:** Since 90 − n(n+1) = (9−n)(10+n), we get p(90) = 8!·18!/10! > 0. Also 90 − a = 729/8.

Then
g(90) = c·(729/8)·p(90) = −(81/9!)·(18!/10!) = −81·C(18,9)/10 = −81·4862 = −393822.

Therefore f(90) − 1/90² = g(90)/90² = −393822/8100 = −2431/50.

The sign checks out on a two-point analogue (f linear through (2, 1/4) and (6, 1/36)), where the same method gives c = −1/18, matching the directly computed leading coefficient.

Solution 1 has the right method and magnitude but drops the sign when it writes g(90) = +9·C(18,8). Solution 2 (192049/4050) and Solution 3 (0) are both incorrect.
